name: Tao-yün
bio: Tao-yün (c. AD 400) was the wife of General Wang Ning-chih. According to Waley the general was so stupid that she finally deserted him. Her poem, “Climbing a Mountain,” imagines a lodging for ever in a hollow among the rocks.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: Climbing a Mountain
poems.author: Tao-yün
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
High rises the Eastern Peak
Soaring up to the blue sky.
Among the rocks--an empty hollow,
Secret, still, mysterious!
Uncarved and unhewn,
Screened by nature with a roof of clouds.
Times and Seasons, what things are you
Bringing to my life ceaseless change?
I will lodge for ever in this hollow
Where Springs and Autumns unheeded pass.
